title: Video Stitching
hints: at any point during stitching, does it matter which specific clip you used to reach your current coverage boundary, or only how far that boundary currently extends?

for every integer second s from 0 to time - 1, find the maximum end value among all clips whose start is at most s and whose end is beyond s - this tells you the farthest you could extend coverage if your current boundary were at s

walk forward from 0, tracking the current guaranteed-covered boundary and the farthest reach seen among all seconds up to that boundary - when your walk reaches the current boundary itself, you must 'use up' a clip: advance the boundary to that farthest reach and increment your clip count
if, at the moment you're forced to extend, the farthest reach found doesn't go past the current boundary at all, no clip can bridge that gap, so full coverage is impossible

why does always jumping to the single farthest reach available (rather than any shorter option) never cost you more clips in total? because reaching farther can only reduce or match how many more forced-extension steps remain, exactly the same reasoning as in the classic jump game - a longer reach dominates a shorter one in every future scenario
commonMistakes: picking clips greedily by their raw length instead of by how far their end extends, which can pick a long but poorly-positioned clip over a shorter, farther-reaching one
forgetting to first check that some clip actually starts at 0, silently treating an uncoverable start as if the algorithm will naturally return -1 without an explicit reachability check
not detecting a coverage gap when the farthest reach found up to the current boundary fails to exceed that boundary, and instead looping forever or under-reporting the clip count

content.problemStatement:
You want to produce a video covering the exact time range [0, `time`]. You have a collection of `clips`, where `clips[i] = [start, end]` represents a clip covering the interval [start, end]. You may use a clip in full or only part of it, and you don't need to use every clip.

**Return the minimum number of clips needed so their combined coverage spans all of [0, `time`], or -1 if it's impossible.**
constraints: each clip is [start, end] with start <= end
clips may overlap, be redundant, or leave gaps
notes: a single clip already covers [0, time] exactly
clips leave a gap somewhere in the middle of [0, time] (impossible)
many overlapping clips where only a few are actually necessary
no clip starts at 0 (impossible, since [0, time] can never begin being covered)

sampleTestCases.explanation: use [0,2] then [1,9] then [8,10]: together they cover [0,2] union [1,9] union [8,10] = [0,10]
the available clips only cover up to time 2, leaving [2,5] with no footage at all

optimal.time: O(n + time), or O(n log n) if sorting instead of bucketing by start
optimal.pattern: for each starting second, precompute the farthest end reachable by any clip beginning there, then greedily extend coverage as far as possible with each clip chosen, like Jump Game II over intervals

bruteForce.approach: try every subset of clips, check whether their union covers [0, time] with no gaps, keep the smallest covering subset
